name: Unimate industrial manipulation at Ewing
description: A programmable industrial manipulator handled hot die-cast parts at a General Motors factory; ASME reports that it placed them in cooling liquid.

impact.note: The first working programmable factory robot, a new capability taken up by manufacturers in several countries, from which industrial robotics grew.

date.basis: The source reports the date for this scoped event or archaeological context.

events.statement: General Motors operated an Unimate at Ewing, New Jersey.

evidence.supports: General Motors operated an Unimate at Ewing, New Jersey.
The source attributes this contribution to general-motors.
ASME attributes the Unimate to inventor George Devol.

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated case currently researched, not a claim of the capability’s original invention or global priority.

caveats: The ASME article is retrospective; competing accounts describe different early tasks, dates and configurations. Specific machine duties require plant records.

research.note: Independent review checked ASME’s account of the 1961 deployment and task; other histories emphasize removal from the die-casting press. Precise task sequence needs further corroboration.
